What's new in Tareekh 2.2

Explain, appeal and ask: AI help for every court order

Tareekh 2.2 adds three AI features to every saved court order: Explain in simple terms (English, Bengali or Hindi), Appeal: where and by when, and Ask about this order. They use the AI service you connect in Settings (Google Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, Qwen or Kimi) with your own API key; without one, Tareekh asks you to connect a service first. The pictures below use a made-up specimen order (T.S. 245/2025, Baruipur).

Explain in simple terms

  • What the court decided, what happens next, what the client must do
  • English, বাংলা or हिन्दी
  • Share with the client on WhatsApp
  • Kept on the phone: opens again offline

Appeal: where and by when

  • Remedy, forum and provision
  • Limitation period and the last date, with days left
  • Time excluded by law and other remedies
  • Add the deadline to your calendar

Ask about this order

  • Any question about the order
  • Follow-up questions in one conversation
  • Answers point to the order's own words
  • Kept with the order
Please note. AI can be wrong, particularly on the appeal forum and limitation (certified-copy time, special Acts, condonation). Treat the Appeal screen as guidance and verify before filing. The order's text and pictures go only to the AI service you chose, and only when you tap one of these items.

How to use it

  1. Settings › Reading with AI: choose the service and paste your API key.
  2. Open a case; under Orders, tap ⋮ next to an order.
  3. Choose Explain in simple terms, Appeal: where and by when or Ask about this order. Switch between them with the tabs at the top.
  4. Share the explanation with your client, or add the appeal deadline to your calendar.

Screen by screen

The order menu

Every saved order now has a ⋮ button. Open and Share are there as before, with three new AI items below them.

  1. 1
    ⋮ on every order

    Tap the three dots next to any order saved under a case.

  2. 2
    Open · Share

    Open the PDF, or share it (WhatsApp, e-mail…), as before. These work without AI and without internet.

  3. 3
    Explain in simple terms

    A plain-language explanation of the order, in English, Bengali or Hindi.

  4. 4
    Appeal: where and by when

    Where the appeal (or other remedy) lies, under which provision, the limitation period and the last date.

  5. 5
    Ask about this order

    A chat about the order: ask anything, and follow-up questions.

No AI connected yet

The three AI items need an AI service. Until one is connected, Tareekh says so and takes you to Settings.

  1. 1
    Connect an AI service first

    Shown when no AI service has been set up in Settings.

  2. 2
    Open Settings

    Goes straight to Settings › Reading with AI.

Connecting an AI service

One setting serves summons reading and the order features. Your own API key; the service bills your own account.

  1. 1
    Reading with AI (optional)

    In Settings. Off until you choose a service.

  2. 2
    AI service

    Google Gemini, OpenAI (ChatGPT), Claude, Qwen or Kimi. Nothing else is offered.

  3. 3
    API key

    Paste the key from that service; tap the eye to check it. It stays on your phone.

  4. 4
    Model

    Filled in for you. Change it only if the service asks you to.

Explain in simple terms

What the court decided, what happens next and what the client must do, in everyday words. The illustration uses a made-up specimen order.

  1. 1
    Language

    English, বাংলা (Bengali) or हिन्दी (Hindi). Each explanation is kept, so it opens again without internet.

  2. 2
    What the court decided

    The result of the order, without legal jargon.

  3. 3
    What you need to do

    Dates and steps for the client, taken from the order itself.

  4. 4
    Share with client

    Send the explanation on WhatsApp or anywhere else.

  5. 5
    The order itself

    Opens the PDF, to check the explanation against the order.

In Bengali (and Hindi)

The same explanation in the client's own language: tap বাংলা or हिन्दी.

  1. 1
    বাংলা

    Bengali explanation of the same order.

  2. 2
    Share with client

    Send it to the client in their language.

Appeal: where and by when

The remedy against the order, the forum, the provision and the time limit, with the last date worked out.

  1. 1
    Remedy and forum

    Which appeal or revision lies, before which court, under which section, Order or Article.

  2. 2
    Last date

    Counted from the order date; days left are shown, in red when fewer than 7.

  3. 3
    Time excluded by law

    E.g. the time taken to get the certified copy, which adds to the period.

  4. 4
    Other remedies

    Review, revision, writ or a fresh application, where they apply.

  5. 5
    Verify before filing

    It is AI guidance, with its confidence shown. Always check the forum and limitation yourself.

  6. 6
    Add deadline to calendar

    An all-day calendar entry on the last date, with alerts a week and a day before.

Ask about this order

Ask questions about the order and follow them up; the conversation is kept with the order.

  1. 1
    Your question

    Type it, or tap a suggestion (what must my client do, any stay, grounds of appeal…).

  2. 2
    The answer

    Quotes the order where it can, and says when the order does not say something.

  3. 3
    Follow-up questions

    Ask as many as you like; the AI remembers the conversation.

2.1 · Search inside Tareekh

From 2.1: search a court from Tareekh's own screen. Case type is picked from the court's list.

  1. 1
    Four ways to search

    Case no., party name, filing (Supreme Court: diary) no. or CNR, for district courts, High Courts and the Supreme Court.

  2. 2
    Case type from the list

    Type a few letters (WPA, CRR, T.S.…) and pick from the court's own list.

  3. 3
    Search

    Tareekh fills in the court's page out of sight.

2.1 · The CAPTCHA, in Tareekh

The court's CAPTCHA picture is shown here; type the answer and the case opens in Tareekh.

  1. 1
    The court's CAPTCHA

    The picture from the court's own page. The refresh button gets a new one.

  2. 2
    Your answer

    Type it and tap Search. The Supreme Court's sum opens a number keypad.

  3. 3
    Court's page

    See the court's website itself at any time.

  4. 4
    Show the court's page instead

    If anything looks wrong, finish the search on the court's own page.

Also in this version

  • From 2.1: search inside Tareekh for district courts, all 25 High Courts and the Supreme Court, with the CAPTCHA shown in the app.
  • Every order of a saved case stays on the phone and opens without internet.
  • Summons, notices and WhatsApp photos can also be read by the same AI service, for the best accuracy.
